beers.name: Oude Geuze
beers.research: Flagship gueuze from Brouwerij 3 Fonteinen. A blend of 1-, 2-, and 3-year-old lambics, unfiltered and unpasteurized, bottle-conditioned for at least 6 months. Spontaneous fermentation with wild yeasts, matured in oak casks. Aromas evolve from vibrant citrus and grassy notes to mellow oak and stone fruit with age. Can be cellared for several decades. Untappd: 4.05/5 (80,000+ ratings). https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-3-fonteinen-oude-geuze/4009
beers.food_pairings: Aged cheeses, oysters, mussels, charcuterie, lemon-dressed seafood
beers.considerations: Bottled 26 Nov 2018. Best before 26 Oct 2038 (printed on bottle). No two bottlings are alike. Cellared properly, this bottle has 12+ years of drinking window remaining.

beers.name: Oude Geuze Cuvee Armand & Gaston
beers.research:
Untappd: blend of 1-, 2-, and 3-year-old traditional lambics from the 2018 season. Spontaneous fermentation, unfiltered and unpasteurized. Named after founders Armand Debelder and Gaston Debelder. 3 Fonteinen notes "no two bottlings are alike" due to barrel selection variables.

Rating: 4.3/5 (32,202 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-3-fonteinen-oude-geuze-cuvee-armand-gaston/1594814)
beers.food_pairings: Mussels, oysters, aged Gouda, charcuterie. Classic gueuze pairing — acidity cuts through rich and fatty foods.
beers.considerations: Based on 2018-season lambics — likely bottled 2019-2020, now 6-7 years post-bottle. Probably at or near peak. "Steadfast adherence to tradition" per 3F. One of the most-rated gueuzes on Untappd.

beers.name: Langste Nacht 2019 | Karwijzaad Op Het Koelschip
beers.research:
Untappd: experimental lambic macerated with caraway seeds on the coolship during the "Longest Night" (2019 harvest). Part of 3 Fonteinen's "Speling van het Lot" (Twist of Fate) small-batch experimental series. Bottled April 13, 2021 with ~12 months weighted average age. One quarter of cereals from the Pajottenland region.

Full Untappd name: SvhL XIV.iii Langste Nacht 2019 | Karwijzaad Op Het Koelschip
Rating: 4.19/5 (505 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-svhl-xiv-iii-langste-nacht-2019-karwijzaad-op-het-koelschip/4805170)
beers.food_pairings: Caraway rye bread, aged Edam, light smoked fish. Caraway spice bridges well with savory herbal flavors.
beers.considerations: "Speling van het Lot" (Twist of Fate) series — extremely limited, experimental. Bottled April 2021 from 2019 harvest. Now ~5 years post-bottle. The caraway seed character (similar to rye bread spice) is distinctive. No longer in production.

beers.name: Tete de Cuvee
beers.research:
Untappd: complex vintage blend — 36% Oude du Ble (16 months in 225L French oak barrels) plus five separate batches of Oude Fermier aged 12-25 months in various French oak vessels. Described as fruit-forward with "sweet nectarine" notes and slight tartness.

Rating: 4.39/5 (1,585 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/side-project-brewing-tete-de-cuvee-vintage-2022/5569618)
beers.food_pairings: Stone fruit desserts, mild aged cheeses, light poultry. The nectarine and stone fruit notes complement delicate flavors.
beers.considerations: Side Project's flagship blend — very highly rated (top 5% on Untappd). Complex multi-component blend from 2022 vintage. Now ~3-4 years post-release, well into its window. No longer in production.

beers.name: Oude Fermier
beers.research:
Untappd: farmhouse ale / saison in the Belgian tradition. The Oude Fermier series is Side Project's flagship Belgian-inspired farmhouse program — multi-barrel blends aged in French oak. The 2022 vintage is rated 4.39/5.

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/side-project-brewing-oude-fermier-vintage-2022/5675248)
beers.food_pairings: Roast chicken, Gruyere, fresh herbs, grilled white fish.
beers.considerations: Side Project is a St. Louis farmhouse brewery revered for Belgian-inspired ales. Oude Fermier is their best-known beer. The 2022 vintage is now ~3-4 years old and well into its window. No longer in production.

beers.name: The Unblended Armagandias
beers.research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale aged 2 years in oak Armagnac barrels, bottled March 2021 ("3/21" Premier Keeper Bottle). De Garde spontaneous ales typically peak 3-8 years post-bottling; Armagnac barrel character integrates beautifully with extended age.

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-the-unblended-armagandias/4434932)
beers.food_pairings: Aged cheeses, charcuterie, duck confit. The Armagnac barrel notes pair well with rich, fatty foods.
beers.considerations: "3/21" in the name refers to the March 2021 bottling date. Now ~5 years post-bottle — likely in prime drinking window. Described as tart and dry with vinous, wine-like qualities and Armagnac barrel notes. No longer in production.

beers.name: The Vintage
beers.research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale aged 4 years in oak barrels before bottling May 2022 — an exclusive Keepers Bottle release. Four years of oak aging gives exceptional depth and stability. Now ~4 years post-bottle; well into its drinking window.

Rating: 4.09/5 (315 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-the-vintage-2018/5152046)
beers.food_pairings: Farmhouse cheeses, roast chicken, mushroom dishes, light charcuterie.
beers.considerations: Quantity ×2. A premium De Garde release — "The Vintage" series represents best-of-year barrels selected by the brewery. Bottled May 2022 after 4 years of aging, meaning this contains 2018 harvest lambic. No longer in production.

beers.name: Sen XXVI
beers.research:
Single wort spelt wheat saison. Open fermented in stainless (May 2023), then aged 15 months in neutral oak barrels before bottling. Whole flower Crystal hops from Kirk family, Willamette Valley Farms. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer Adam Paysse note (from Floodland bottle log): "Drinking great now, will continue to do so for some time. I imagine this will evolve in the bottle, best before Spring 2028."

Flavor profile: balanced acidity and bitterness, distinct Brett character that remains bright and aromatic, floral with orange-leaning citrus from Crystal hops.

Sources:
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log - Sen XXVI](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
[Sen XXVI Review - rihobeer.com](https://rihobeer.com/en/floodland-brewing-sen-xxvi-artisanal-saison-combining-water-like-mouthfeel-with-complex-fermentation-aromas/)
beers.food_pairings: Soft-rind cheeses (Brie, Camembert), raw oysters or shellfish, roast chicken, spring vegetables, stone fruit desserts
beers.considerations: "Sen" = Senescence; XXVI means this is the 26th in the series. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar. Bright, floral Brett character will soften and integrate further over the aging window. ABV 6.37%.

beers.name: MMXXIV Gruner Veltliner
beers.research: Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 01/16/2025, ABV 8.29%. Brewer notes best within 18 months of bottling (by ~July 2026), with summer 2027 as the absolute outer limit.
beers.considerations: Higher ABV Floodland blend. Adam Paysse notes best within 18 months of bottling (i.e., by ~July 2026), though summer 2027 is the outer limit.

beers.name: I Want to Be Known
beers.research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 05/29/2025, ABV 4.89%. "Best before fall 2028. Drink fresh."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.considerations: A lighter Floodland release. Adam Paysse recommends drinking fresh — no extended aging benefit. Drink before fall 2028.

beers.name: MMXXIII/MMXXIV True-Nature
beers.research:
From Untappd / Floodland: blend of biodynamic Kerner grape pomace, organic Balaton cherries, and organic red raspberries from the 2023-2024 harvests. Refermented in bottle with organic cane sugar. Bottled 06/12/2025. Best consumed before summer 2027.

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.considerations: Untappd community Gold Award 2026. Named after Ursula K. LeGuin quote. Your beers.md listed this as MMXXII/MMXXIv — Untappd confirms the blend is 2023/2024 vintages.

beers.name: MMXXIV Flowers of the Field
beers.research:
Farmhouse ale with entirely native fermentation of Chardonnay grapes (French Creek Vineyard, Yakima River Valley) and Pinot Noir grapes (Johan Vineyards, Van Duzer Corridor), 2024 harvest. Blended open and barrel-fermented saison. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer note: "Conditioned in the bottle for 6+ months prior to release and is drinking great. It should continue to drink well for several years, but I don't think aging will improve it. Best before 2029."

Sources:
[Untappd - MMXXIV Flowers of the Field](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-mmxxiv-flowers-of-the-field-2024-harvest/6641152)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.food_pairings: Brie and triple-crème cheeses, roast salmon, spring pea dishes, herb-roasted chicken, white peach tart
beers.considerations: Brewer explicitly states aging will NOT improve this beer — drink it now through 2028. The Chardonnay and Pinot Noir grape blend gives this a wine-like character. French Creek Vineyard (Yakima) + Johan Vineyards (Van Duzer Corridor, OR) are both highly regarded sources for Floodland.

beers.name: Monarchist
beers.research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 10/31/2024, ABV 6.12%. "Will improve the next 12+ months." Best before fall 2028.

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.considerations: A Floodland flagship blend. Adam Paysse notes continued improvement through at least October 2025, peaking before fall 2028.

beers.name: Vesper
beers.research: Table beer from Holy Mountain Brewing (Seattle, WA). Pilsner malt, flaked rye and wheat; hopped with Styrian Golding and Cascade; fermented with Belgian yeast and conditioned with Brettanomyces. Low-ABV but complex — the Brett adds earthy, funky depth. Won Silver in 2026 Untappd Community Awards. No 2025-specific Untappd listing; current bottlings are logged to the base entry. https://untappd.com/b/holy-mountain-brewing-vesper/2515677
beers.food_pairings: Light charcuterie, soft cheeses, roast chicken, grain salads
beers.considerations: 2025 bottling, likely summer. Exact bottle date unknown — estimated July 2025. Brett-conditioned table beer; drink young to fresh but will develop further over 2-3 years. 2 bottles in cellar.

beers.name: Cherry Field Blend
beers.research:
Oak-fermented farmhouse saison refermented on foraged Cornelian cherries, organic Balaton, Montmorency, and Van cherries. Bottle conditioned with organic cane sugar.

Brewer note (Untappd): "Field Blend is an exercise in embracing time as a source of wonder rather than an instrument of control." Best before summer 2028.

Note: The 2024 Cherry Field Blend (bottled Oct 2024) had a best-before of early 2027 — this 2025 bottling extends that window to summer 2028.

Sources:
[Untappd - Cherry Field Blend (2025)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-cherry-field-blend-2025/6641153)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.food_pairings: Aged gouda or comté, duck with cherry sauce, lamb chops, dark chocolate tart, charcuterie with sour cherry preserves
beers.considerations: Bottle conditioned — expect light sediment. Four cherry varieties: Cornelian (foraged), Balaton, Montmorency, Van. The cherry character in Floodland Field Blends tends to integrate and deepen with age rather than fade. Drinking great now and through summer 2028.

beers.name: Temps & Poivre
beers.research:
Untappd: "A Spontaneous Wild Ale with Black Pepper Aged in Oak Barrels for Six Years. Bottled 11/24 Premier Keeper Bottle." Six years of oak aging predates bottling — the base lambic is highly developed. Black pepper integrates well with extended time. Allow at least 12 months of bottle rest.

Rating: 4.28/5 (98 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-temps-poivre-11-24/6194067)
beers.food_pairings: Spiced meat dishes, aged gouda, dark chocolate, roasted vegetables.
beers.considerations: "11/24" in the name denotes the November 2024 bottling. Despite 6 years of barrel aging, bottle conditioning benefits from at least 1 year of rest before opening. The black pepper spice character is "well-integrated" per reviewers.

beers.name: Filaree (2025)
beers.research: Brewer's official cellar notes state the beer has been conditioned 6+ months pre-release and is 'drinking great' now, with recommendation to 'drink well for several years' but aging won't improve it significantly. Official 'Best before 2029' establishes the drink_by window. Bottled 2025-12-11.
beers.considerations:
This beer was created using 2025 harvest Santa Rosa, Shiro, Elephant Heart, Howard's Miracle, and Green Gage plums grown organically in the Okanogan Valley by JC and Amber Kaufmann at Filaree Fruit. The plums were refermented with barrel aged spelt saison and wheat saison.

This bottling was made in an attempt to showcase the fruit grown by the Kaufmann family at Filaree. Refermented to condition in the bottle.

Bottled 12/11/2025

Conditioned with: Organic sugar.
Cellar: This has been conditioned in the bottle for 6+ months prior to release and is drinking great. It should continue to drink well for several years, but I don't think aging will improve it significantly. Best before 2029.

beers.name: Between Two Toms
beers.research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale with chamomile flowers, aged in oak gin barrels 2-4 years, then blended with Voodoo Brewing. "Moderate acidity, but the botanicals and chamomile are poppin." A collaboration beer — unusual gin barrel provenance gives it distinct botanical character.

Rating: 4.17/5 (33 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-between-two-toms/6458919)
beers.food_pairings: Light seafood, soft cheeses, cucumber dishes. The chamomile and gin botanicals work with delicate flavors.
beers.considerations: Collaboration with Voodoo Brewing. The gin barrel origin is unusual for a wild ale — expect juniper and botanical notes alongside the spontaneous funk. Relatively recent release with limited check-ins.

beers.name: Transits and Occultations (2026)
beers.research: Brewer's cellar notes (highest authority) state the beer was 'drinking nicely at 4 months in the bottle' (suggesting May 2026) but 'should really peak this summer/fall' and 'drink great through summer 2029.' Bottled 2026-01-15.
beers.considerations:
Ale Fermented in Oak

Transits and Occultations is a blend of mixed-culture saison inspired by stories of 19th and 20th century Belgian and French farm beers.

2026 bottling. This blend was constructed of puncheon aged saison brewed in the spring of 2024 with malted 'Bere' barley from Palouse Heritage along with two types each of spelt and wheat. It was hopped with a blend of new and old world whole cone flowers, and fermented with a culture of wild and appropriated yeasts.

This beer was refermented to condition in the bottle.

Bottled 01/15/2026

Conditioned with: Organic sugar.
Cellar: Drinking nicely at 4 months in the bottle, but should really peak this summer/fall. As with any longer aged puncheon saison I'd expect it to drink great through summer 2029.

beers.name: Ill Fate
beers.research:
Blended saison refermented on organic red raspberries from Sidhu Farms, Puyallup River Valley. Three-component blend: spelt saison (March 2024, aged in acacia wood) + spelt and wheat saisons (April and December 2024, aged in neutral oak). Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer note (from Untappd/bottle log): "This is young-ish in the bottle and will continue to improve for the next few months if you keep it at room temperature. Should be at its best June-October 2026, drink by summer 2028."

Sources:
[Untappd - Ill Fate (2025 Harvest)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-ill-fate-2025-harvest/6641155)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.food_pairings: Fresh raspberry desserts, aged chèvre, duck confit, charcuterie with fruit preserves, dark chocolate
beers.considerations: Very young — bottled Nov 2025, just ~5 months old. Best enjoyed after June 2026 per brewer. Bottle conditioned, expect light sediment. Acacia wood aging is unusual and adds a subtle honeyed, almost floral wood note not found in neutral oak beers.

beers.name: MMXXIV-MMXXV That-Which-Is (2024 and 2025 Harvest)
beers.research: No specific drinking window published for this beer. Estimated 2024-01 to 2025-01 based on standard saison aging characteristics. Floodland Brewing typically focuses on mixed-culture, bottle-conditioned saisons designed for fresh drinking with aging potential; flagship saisons from this brewery generally maintain quality for 12 months post-release.
beers.considerations:
"In later years it occasionally happened that I awoke in the night and the stars were so real and advanced so convincingly that I could not understand how people managed to lose so much of the world"
(Rainer Maria Rilke)

2024 and 2025 harvest. This beer was made using saison refermented with 2024 Mourvedre and Syrah grapes from French Creek Vineyards in the Yakima River Valley. After aging over-vintage that beer was further refermented on 2025 organic Balaton cherries from the Old Weddle Farm courtesy of OPMA, and organic blackberries from Sidhu Farms in the Puyallup River Valley.

This beer was refermented to condition in the bottle.

Bottled 02/05/2026

Conditioned with: Organic cane sugar.
Cellar: Still on its ascent. Of all the beers in this release this is the one which I think will most benefit from additional (warm) aging in bottle. It's drinking nicely right now but I think it'll really start to hit its stride late summer/fall '26, and probably not peak until spring 2027

beers.name: Winesap
beers.research: From Floodland's official Untappd cellar note: expects the beer won't peak for at least a year until fall 2026, and should drink well until at least 2028 if not longer. Bottled 07/10/2025.

beers.name: Saint Lamvinus
beers.research: Cantillon Saint Lamvinus 2024 vintage. Blend of lambics aged 16-18 months on merlot, grenache noir, and syrah grapes. lambic.info confirms Saint Lamvinus is bottled mid-October to late-November each year; 2024-11 used as bottling estimate. No official drink window published. Estimated 2026-11 to 2032-11 based on grape lambic aging characteristics (2yr after / 8yr by from bottling).
beers.food_pairings: Aged red wine cheese, charcuterie, duck, venison.
beers.considerations: Younger than the 2023 — allow more bottle time. Community reviews explicitly suggest not rushing this one. Expect peak around 2027-2030.

beers.name: The Broken Truck Grande Cuvée
beers.research: The Broken Truck Grande Cuvee is a wild ale by de Garde Brewing. No official drinking window is published by the brewery. Based on the lambic-inspired character and Brett complexity typical of de Garde barrel-aged spontaneous ales, an estimated drinking window of 2-5 years from bottling (November 2024) has been applied: drink after November 2026, drink by November 2029.

beers.name: Saint Lamvinus
beers.research:
Untappd: "Maceration of different grape varieties (merlot, grenache noir, syrah) in two-year-old lambic. Beer with a taste evolution. Bottled 7 November 2023."

Cantillon Saint Lamvinus is one of the brewery's most sought-after releases — a lambic refermented on red wine grapes. The grape tannins and acidity interplay with the lambic character over years of bottle conditioning. High ABV (7.5%) and grape content support long aging.

Rating: 4.28/5 (2,232 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-saint-lamvinus-2023/5637350)
beers.food_pairings: Aged red wine cheese (Comté, Manchego), charcuterie, duck, venison. The vinous character pairs beautifully with food that normally accompanies red wine.
beers.considerations: One of Cantillon's most complex and age-worthy releases. The 2023 was bottled November 2023 — recommend allowing 3 years before opening (fall 2026 or later). No longer in production.

beers.name: Sang Bleu
beers.research:
Untappd: previously known as "Camerise Lambic," rebranded as Sang Bleu (French for "Blue Blood") with new artwork by artist Ammo. A lambic blend with haskap (blue honeysuckle) berries. Brewer: "powerful and very fruit-forward, but still maintains a nice, mellow balance between acidity and astringency."

Rating: 4.21/5 (2,418 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-sang-bleu-2025/6217278)
beers.food_pairings: Blue cheese, duck breast, lamb, dark chocolate. The haskap berry acidity plays well with rich, savory flavors.
beers.considerations: Haskap (blue honeysuckle) is relatively unusual in lambic production — expect blueberry and dark berry notes with good acidity. The rebranding from Camerise Lambic is cosmetic. 2025 vintage — allow 2 years before opening.

beers.name: Magic Lambic
beers.research: Cantillon's official cellar notes state 'allow ~2 years before opening' for the 2025 vintage Magic Lambic (bottled 2025-11). This overrides the prior estimate. Applying the 2-year guidance: drink_after = 2027-11, drink_by = 2032-11 (extending the fruit lambic window by ~2 years from bottling per brewer recommendation).
beers.food_pairings: Dark chocolate, raspberry tart, soft cheeses. Classic framboise pairings.
beers.considerations: Cantillon's framboise program. Magic Lambic is one of their more fruit-forward releases. 2025 vintage — allow ~2 years before opening.

beers.name: Ashanti
beers.research: Cantillon's official bottling notes state 'Allow ~2 years before opening' for the 2025 vintage Ashanti (bottled 2025-11). This yields drink_after of 2027-11. Estimated drink_by of 2032-11 based on spiced lambic aging (6yr window from bottling), as pepper aromatics will develop complexity over time while remaining enjoyable.
beers.food_pairings: Spiced dishes, grilled meats, aged Gouda. The pepper character pairs with savory, warming food.
beers.considerations: Ashanti pepper (Piper guineense) — also known as West African pepper or Benin pepper — gives warm, peppery, slightly woody aromatics. 2025 vintage. Allow ~2 years before opening. One of Cantillon's more unusual specialty releases.

beers.name: The Broken Truck: Rocks District (11/25)
beers.research: No official window published. Estimated 2027-11–2032-11 based on spontaneous wild ale/lambic aging characteristics and bottling date 2025-11. de Garde's spontaneous ales typically age 1-7+ years in bottle, with traditional lambic guidelines suggesting consumption within 2-7 years post-bottling for optimal complexity.

beers.name: The Broken Truck
beers.research: No official drinking window is published by de Garde Brewing. Based on style (lambic-inspired spontaneous wild ale) and bottling date (December 2025), an estimated window of 2-7 years from bottling has been applied: drink after December 2027, drink by December 2032. The beer is a blend from three different years of barrel-aged components, suggesting it has already undergone significant oak maturation and may reward extended cellaring.
beers.considerations:
Shortly after we started distributing, we had our cursed old brewery truck break down while carrying a load of kegs to our distributor. Our distributor was about to close for the weekend, and we had no way to get them there in time, and nowhere to store them in good condition during the opressively hot weather. As is our habit during times of stress, we sought a cold beer at the newly opened taproom and growler station around the corner, Tin Bucket. After chatting with the owner, he expressed his disappointment at not being able to get our beer. To cut it short, he and his partner bought the entire truckload, saving not just the beer, but quite literally our business. 

This beer is for them. We worked with them to blend this from three different years of our lambic inspired barrels. We chose a blend with a beautiful and expressive Brett character that has only blossomed during its extended conditioning. Our favorite beer to date.

beers.name: Oude Kriek
beers.research:
Untappd: traditional lambic Kriek using Schaarbeekse cherries — the rare sour morello variety prized for kriek production. Described as "raspberry-like Schaarbeekse Kriek" with "sweet-tart blackberry depth" and "perfect acidity/complexity balance."

Rating: 4.12/5 (2,172 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/geuzestekerij-de-cam-oude-kriek/66369)
beers.food_pairings: Dark chocolate, duck, venison, cherry-glazed pork. The kriek acidity loves rich, game-forward dishes.
beers.considerations: Best-before date printed on bottle: 12/10/2034. De Cam is a traditional Pajottenland blending house (geuzestekerij) — they blend and age lambic from other producers. Schaarbeekse cherries are extremely rare and valued for their high acidity and complex flavor.

beers.name: 2026 Dead as Dreams
beers.research: Pale, refreshing, and aromatic — a classic Floodland bottle. Second release in a series that began with 'Cut Their Grain and Place Fire Therein.' Not yet listed on Untappd or the Floodland bottle log as of 2026-07-24 (very recent mailing-list release). No official drink window published. Estimated drink_after 2026-07 (fresh, low-ABV pale style, drink young per Floodland pattern for similar-ABV releases like I Want to Be Known and Nothing Ever Begins) and drink_by 2028-07 (~2 years, consistent with the brewery's lighter/fresher bottlings).
beers.food_pairings: Light, refreshing pale saison — pairs well with fresh cheeses, salads, and light seafood.
beers.considerations: 2 bottles.

beers.name: MMXXI Muscat
beers.research:
Farmhouse ale / saison primary fermented on native-fermented Muscat grapes from Palimpsest Vineyard, Newberg, OR. Grape harvest: Sep 25, 2021. Bottled: Mar 3, 2022 with raw honey from Cougar Canyon Apiary.

No official brewer drink window published. Drink window (2024-03-01 to 2027-03-01) is my recommendation based on:
- Comparable MMXXI-series Floodland releases (Rhone, No Echoes)
- Muscat aromatics (rose, orange blossom, stone fruit) are most expressive at 2-4 years post-bottling; brett character continues developing
- Untappd check-ins from 2024-2025 describe it as "smooth, grape peel, light funk" -- still tracking well at 4 years
- ABV 7.44% supports extended cellaring vs. lighter Floodland releases

Sources:
[Untappd - MMXXI Muscat (2021)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-mmxxi-muscat-2021/4953395)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.food_pairings: Fresh goat cheese or burrata, stone fruit (peach, apricot, nectarine), lightly spiced dishes (Thai, Vietnamese, Moroccan), grilled fish, crème brûlée or tarte tatin
beers.considerations: Bottle conditioned with raw honey -- expect light sediment, store upright. Grapes from Palimpsest Vineyard (Newberg, OR); honey from Cougar Canyon Apiary. No longer in production. Rated 4.39/5 on Untappd (366 ratings).

beers.name: Nothing Ever Begins
beers.research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 04/24/2025, ABV 6.99%. "Best before spring 2027. Drink fresh."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
beers.considerations: Relatively short window per Adam Paysse — drink before spring 2027. No extended aging benefit.
beers.imbibe_notes: Was OK, definitely tasted the wine notes

beers.name: Transits and Occultations (2026)
beers.research: No official drinking window published for this beer. Estimated based on standard saison aging characteristics: assuming a 2026 vintage (bottled 2026), a drinkable window of 2026–2027 reflects typical farmhouse ale aging. Floodland beers are bottle-conditioned and designed to develop complexity over 6-12 months.
beers.considerations:
Ale Fermented in Oak

Transits and Occultations is a blend of mixed-culture saison inspired by stories of 19th and 20th century Belgian and French farm beers.

2026 bottling. This blend was constructed of puncheon aged saison brewed in the spring of 2024 with malted 'Bere' barley from Palouse Heritage along with two types each of spelt and wheat. It was hopped with a blend of new and old world whole cone flowers, and fermented with a culture of wild and appropriated yeasts.

This beer was refermented to condition in the bottle.

Bottled 01/15/2026

Conditioned with: Organic sugar.
Cellar: Drinking nicely at 4 months in the bottle, but should really peak this summer/fall. As with any longer aged puncheon saison I'd expect it to drink great through summer 2029.
beers.imbibe_notes: Very very nice, straightforward saison, slightly funky.  Look forward to tasting in 2028

beers.name: Filaree (2025)
beers.research: No official cellaring window published for 2025 Filaree. Estimated based on Floodland Brewing's established aging patterns for barrel-aged, fruit-refermented saisons. The brewery's similar heavily-fruited saisons (e.g., Nothing Ever Begins variants) typically peak 12-18 months post-bottling and remain cellarworthy 3-5 years. Bottling 2025-01 (assumed).
beers.considerations:
This beer was created using 2025 harvest Santa Rosa, Shiro, Elephant Heart, Howard's Miracle, and Green Gage plums grown organically in the Okanogan Valley by JC and Amber Kaufmann at Filaree Fruit. The plums were refermented with barrel aged spelt saison and wheat saison.

This bottling was made in an attempt to showcase the fruit grown by the Kaufmann family at Filaree. Refermented to condition in the bottle.

Bottled 12/11/2025

Conditioned with: Organic sugar.
Cellar: This has been conditioned in the bottle for 6+ months prior to release and is drinking great. It should continue to drink well for several years, but I don't think aging will improve it significantly. Best before 2029.

wines.name: Brunello di Montalcino BIO
wines.research: Brunello's Sangiovese Grosso demands extended bottle ageing to allow its firm tannins, vivid acidity and oak influence to harmonise. Le Chiuse's organically farmed fruit gradually unfolds tertiary notes of leather, spice and earth across 8 to 20 years, achieving remarkable complexity while retaining its characteristic freshness.
wines.considerations:
Young: In its youth, the wine displays bright cherry and cranberry fruit, a delicate floral lift and lively acidity, supported by firm, grippy tannins and subtle hints of vanilla and herbs derived from oak ageing and extended maceration.
Ripe: At peak maturity, it reveals layered aromas and flavours of dried cherry, plum, leather, tobacco and forest floor. The tannins become silky and well integrated, the spice seamlessly woven through the palate, culminating in a long, savoury finish underpinned by persistent, refreshing acidity.
Storage: Store at 12–15°C with 60–70% relative humidity, maintaining a steady temperature and keeping bottles away from direct light and vibration. Lay bottles on their side to keep the cork moist and ensure a proper seal.

wines.name: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Riserva
wines.research: Boscarelli Vino Nobile Riserva is built on concentrated Sangiovese with firm tannins and bright acidity. It rewards medium to long bottle ageing, developing tertiary complexity after several years while retaining enough structure to be enjoyed for up to two decades.
wines.considerations:
Young: Bright cherry and cranberry fruit with a floral lift, lively acidity and firm, grippy tannins. Oak spice and leather notes remain assertive and forward.
Ripe: Ripe cherry, plum and dried herbs emerge alongside leather, tobacco and savoury spice. Tannins soften and integrate, acidity finds balance, and the finish is long and complex.
Storage: Store at 12–14°C with 60–70% humidity, away from light and vibration, bottles laid horizontal.

wines.name: Pinot Noir
wines.research: Cool-climate Freycinet Pinot Noir is approachable in its youth but rewards short-term cellaring with added complexity; best enjoyed once initial reductive notes have softened and before tertiary characters begin to dominate.
wines.considerations:
Young: Bright cranberry and wild cherry fruit, lifted floral aromatics, brisk acidity and fine-grained tannins; lively, fresh and well-suited to the table.
Ripe: Riper cherry and plum fruit, savoury earth and forest mushroom notes, well-integrated oak and silky tannins with greater length and complexity.
Storage: Store at 12–15°C with stable humidity, away from light and vibration, bottles laid horizontal.

wines.name: Brunello di Montalcino, Vigna Montosoli
wines.research: Montosoli Brunello's concentrated Sangiovese, firm tannins, and bright acidity demand extended cellaring; 10–25 years allows tertiary complexity to unfold while preserving lively fruit character.
wines.considerations:
Young: When young: tight, austere tannins with vibrant acidity; primary aromas of sour cherry, cranberry, dried rose, cedar, and firm oak structure.
Ripe: At peak: refined, silky tannins with seamlessly integrated oak; rich notes of dried cherry, leather, tobacco, warm spice, and dried herbs, concluding in a long, savory finish.
Storage: Store at 12–14°C with approximately 70% humidity, in darkness, bottles laid horizontal, and with minimal vibration.
